title: RpcQuery
description: Browser-connect v0.4 read-only JSON-RPC proxy (`rpc_query`, wire message over the connect-serve socket — same lightweight-message convention as connect_request/permission_revoke, which also carry no schema_version/request_id envelope). Whitelist-only — the wallet forwards nothing outside a small, hardcoded set of pure chain-state reads (see properties/method) — executed only against the session's granted chain via the wallet's own RPC endpoint, never a caller-supplied one. Capsule-bearing (asserts origin/capsule_id) so it requires host attestation (ADR-013) exactly like connect_request/transaction_request, and requires an active permission grant (read-only class suffices) for the requesting capsule on the requested chain. No signing consequence: this path never reaches decode/policy/vault. Per-query audit events are deliberately not emitted (see ADR-019) — connection-level enforcement (attestation, permission, whitelist, size caps) still applies on every call. This top-level shape is the request; the response is `$defs/response`.

origin.description: dapp origin URL, same identity model as connect_request

capsule_id.description: browser capsule identity, same identity model as connect_request

method.description: STRICT hardcoded whitelist — not caller-extensible. Anything else is refused (malformed_or_unsupported) before it is ever forwarded.

params.description: positional JSON-RPC params for `method`, exactly as EIP-1193/eth-JSON-RPC defines them (a JSON array; absent/null treated as no params)

response.description: on success: {"message":"rpc_query_response","result":<raw JSON-RPC result>}. Refusals use the transport's existing {"message":"error","code":...,"detail":...} shape (malformed_or_unsupported for off-whitelist methods, size_cap_exceeded, unknown_chain, permission_required, attestation_required, identity_required, rpc_unavailable) — never a bespoke error shape for this message kind.

result.description: the raw JSON-RPC result, forwarded verbatim
